format.note: 16 clubs play home and away (30 rounds), then split into 1st-6th, 7th-10th and 11th-16th; each group plays once more, so the top and bottom groups reach 35 rounds and the middle group stops at 33

playoff.note: 14th plays the winner of a one-off tie between the Cymru North and Cymru South runners-up for the last Cymru Premier place; 15th and 16th go down directly
champion promoted if it holds a Tier 1 licence; the runner-up meets the Cymru South runner-up, and that winner then meets the Cymru Premier 14th

boundaries.note: Cymru North and Cymru South each send their champion up (licence required). The two runners-up meet in a one-off; that winner then plays the Cymru Premier 14th for the last top-flight place, so exactly one of {14th, tier-2 play-off winner} is in the league next season. 15th and 16th are relegated directly and are placed in North or South by geography.

notes: Sizes and levels match our rows and are solid: 16/16/16 is the new shape from 2026-27 (the Cymru Premier expanded from 12 to 16 for this season, taking 3 clubs from each of Cymru North and Cymru South in 2026). Confidence is medium only because the split/play-off mechanics come from a single encyclopaedic source (the Cymru Premier article citing BBC/FAW) and this is the first season of that format; no FAW page could be read directly to cross-check. WAL2 and WA2S are parallel regional divisions at level 2 and do not exchange clubs with each other - clubs are placed north or south by geography, and unlike England's National League North/South there is no balancing transfer between them. Level 2 relegates into the four Ardal Leagues (level 3), which is outside our dataset; the exact number of Ardal relegations was not verified and is not modelled. Cups and European qualification (including the 2nd-7th Conference League play-offs) excluded.
